newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank leaves money policy unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank leaves money policy unchanged.

text.p: The central bank board decided on Saturday to leave Taiwan's monetary policy unchanged and set a November 14 meeting to further review the island's reserve system, vice governor Liang Cheng-chin said.

In describing the morning board meeting just after its conclusion, Liang made no mention of adjustments to monetary policy and said the November 14 meeting would focus on liberalisation of Taiwan's reserve system.
"The change of the reserve system involves complicated measures so we will discuss these during the board meeting," Liang said at a noon news conference.
Liang said the international trend was to lower banks' reserve requirements and raise the liquidity ration but that no specific decisions with regard to Taiwan's own reserve system had been made.
The meeting outcome was in line with market expectations.

Liang and other officials had said as recently as October 11 that Saturday's meeting would have "nothing to do" with adjusting monetary policy, but would focus instead on reform of the reserve system.
Central bank officals have noted in recent days that current interbank money rates were low and foreign exchange rates stable, implying Taiwan's monetary policy needed no adjustment.
Bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on October 7 that liquidity had become "slightly too loose" but that the bank would maintain an "appropriately loose" monetary policy.
This meant preventing interest rates from dropping "too low so as not to hurt the interests of most depositors", he said.
Sheu said the bank's loose monetary policy had shown itself to be no "cure-all" for Taiwan's slowing economy.
Sheu noted that five consecutive decreases in commercial banks' reserve requirements since mid-1995 had made money more accessible -- but failed to reignite private investment.
Further liberalisation was needed to bring unregulated or illegal financing operations into legal channels, he said.
